message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became known for his combination of size, athleticism, court vision, and scoring ability—an all‑round game that made him a perennial All‑Star and MVP candidate. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights of his career include:

- **NBA Championships**: Four titles (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013 with the Heat; 2020 with the Lakers).
- **MVP Awards**: Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and one Finals MVP (2020).
- **All‑NCAA**: 17‑time NBA All‑Star, 13‑time All‑Defensive Team selection, and multiple All‑NBA First‑Team honors.
- **Scoring & Playmaking**: He has consistently posted high points per game averages and is among the league’s leaders in assists and rebounds for a forward.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron—a public charter school aimed at helping at-risk children. He is also a media entrepreneur, having founded SpringHill Entertainment and producing films and television shows. His influence extends into business ventures, endorsements, and social activism, making him a prominent figure both within and outside the world of sports.
